name: superlite
description: Lightweight Claude Code skills for the build lifecycle: one approval gate, parallel waves, short reports
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for Superlite skills:

- When a Superlite skill says to ask the user, ask clarifying questions, present options, or wait for the user's choice (`AskUserQuestion`), call Kimi Code's `AskUserQuestion` tool. Do not render those choices as plain assistant text unless `AskUserQuestion` is unavailable or the session is in auto permission mode.
- For `AskUserQuestion`, provide up to 4 questions with 2-4 concrete options each when possible. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with `(Recommended)`.
- When a Superlite skill says to keep a todo or plan list (one todo per wave, update plan tools), use Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool.
- When a Superlite skill says to dispatch an agent (`Agent` with a `superlite:*` `subagent_type`: `implementer`, `implementer-haiku`, `package-reviewer`, `final-reviewer`, `fixer-sonnet`, `fixer-sonnet-high` or `fixer-opus`, plus `model` and `effort`), Kimi Code has no such plugin agents. Call Kimi Code's `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "coder"` and a short `description`. Put the full text of the plugin's `agents/<name>.md` (without its frontmatter) followed by the brief into `prompt`. Do not pass the superlite subagent type names, and do not pass `general-purpose` as `subagent_type`.
- Kimi Code has no per-call `model` or `effort`. Keep the tier in mind (implementer, package-reviewer, fixer-sonnet: mid-tier medium effort; fixer-sonnet-high: mid-tier high effort; implementer-haiku: cheapest tier, high effort; final-reviewer, fixer-opus: top tier high effort; tests run via `sl run_tests`, not an agent) and use a cheaper configured model only if Kimi Code exposes one.
- For read-only codebase exploration (`subagent_type: Explore`), use `Agent` with `subagent_type: "explore"`. For read-only planning, use `subagent_type: "plan"`.
- Send follow-ups to a running agent (`SendMessage`) by resuming that same agent if `Agent` supports it; otherwise dispatch a new `coder` agent with the earlier report and the new instructions in its prompt.
- Keep dependent steps sequential. Dispatch a whole wave of independent agents in one message, or use `run_in_background: true` when background agents are available.
- When a skill refers to the `Skill` tool, use Kimi Code's native `Skill` tool.
- Use Kimi Code's `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `FetchURL`, `WebSearch`, and MCP tools by their actual exposed names. To search file contents use `Grep`; to find files use `Glob`; to fetch a URL use `FetchURL`; to search the web use `WebSearch`.

interface.shortDescription: Lean planning, TDD, debugging, and delivery workflows for coding agents
interface.longDescription: Use Superlite to guide agent work through brainstorming with one approval gate, contract-style implementation plans, parallel-wave subagent execution, test-driven development, systematic debugging, and finish-the-branch workflows.
